next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Queue Project Name: Inline Creation UX Polish & Project Templates
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Build upon the project_name field in the Add to Queue form by adding: (1) Project templates — when creating a new project via the 'Create' button, allow users to select from predefined templates (e.g., 'ML Research', 'Web App', 'Data Pipeline') that pre-populate the artifacts/research/tests directories with relevant starter files and README stubs. (2) Project metadata tagging — add the ability to tag projects with categories/labels at creation time, stored in a workspace/.project_meta.json file. (3) Recent projects history — surface the last 5 used project names in a 'Recent' section of the datalist dropdown. (4) Project health indicator — show a small colored dot next to existing project names in the datalist indicating whether the project has active missions in the queue. All changes should be consistent across both the Add to Queue form and the edit modal.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The current mission established the foundation (project_name field + directory creation). The natural next step is to make project creation richer and more useful: templates reduce boilerplate, metadata enables filtering/organization, recency surfaces the most relevant projects quickly, and health indicators give situational awareness. These are all incremental improvements on the same UI surface with clear user value.

final_report.summary: Successfully added a project_name field with autocomplete, validation warning, and 'Create New Project' button to the 'Add to Queue' / Create Mission form in the AtlasForge dashboard. The implementation mirrors the existing project_name functionality in the edit modal, providing a consistent user experience where project_name can be set at mission creation time rather than only after queuing. All 20 tests (12 functional + 8 adversarial) passed with an epistemic score of 0.90. Live system verification confirmed all endpoints and UI elements are present, functional, and secure.
key_achievements: Added project_name input field (id='queue-add-project-name') with HTML5 datalist autocomplete to the 'Add to Queue' form
Implemented fetchQuickAddProjects() which populates the datalist from the existing /api/queue/workspace-projects endpoint on widget initialization
Implemented onQueueProjectNameInput() validation that shows an amber non-blocking warning when a typed project name does not exist in the workspace
Implemented createQueueProject() which calls new POST /api/queue/create-project endpoint to create workspace directories (with artifacts/research/tests subdirs) on demand
Added new /api/queue/create-project Flask endpoint with strict regex validation (^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+$) blocking path traversal and injection attacks
Updated quickAddEnhanced() to read project_name from the queue form's own dedicated field (not the R&D panel field), and to send it in the add-enhanced payload
Rebuilt JS/CSS bundle to include all new functionality
All 20 tests passed (12 functional + 8 adversarial); live endpoint validation confirmed
challenges_overcome: Identified that quickAddEnhanced() was previously reading from the R&D panel's #project-name-input field instead of a queue-specific field — fixed by redirecting reads to #queue-add-project-name
Ensured the 'Create' button appears conditionally only for new project names and disappears after creation, requiring careful datalist state inspection
Bundle rebuild required to propagate JS changes to dist/ — handled via npm run build with version hash management
Path traversal security: validated that regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+$ correctly blocks all ../  variants, null bytes, control chars, and XSS payloads in the create-project endpoint
lessons_learned: When extending existing UI patterns (edit modal → add form), map all state changes carefully: datalist population timing, button visibility toggling, input clearing after submit
HTML5 datalist autocomplete is low-friction for project name suggestions but requires JavaScript to detect whether a typed value matches an option (options array comparison)
Security-first regex for directory names (^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]+$) is simple and effective — apply it at the backend, never rely solely on frontend validation
Non-blocking warnings (amber hints) are the right UX pattern for 'new project' validation — blocking submission for a valid use case (creating a new project) would be anti-user
Functional + adversarial test pairing is highly effective: functional tests prove spec compliance, adversarial tests prove security hardness
